_comment: Symbol-size ratchet pins (#1155). MEASURED values, never round ceilings. Taken at the bench's own flags (Release = -O3 -DNDEBUG -std=c++23) on the toolchain named below; sizes are compiler-bound, so the gate refuses to compare across toolchains. Re-pin with: python3 bench/symbol_ratchet.py --build bench/build --pins bench/symbol_ratchet.json --emit

symbols.note: RE-PINNED 384 -> 427 (+43 B) by RFC-0028 slice 7 (one callback idiom, D10). No per-edge work was added: a HANDLER target is now handed the published block by reference (the adopting store_value overload calls the noinline handler_write directly, no try_rope clone), and with that clone path gone from graph.cpp GCC 13.3 re-partitions the TU's inline budget and inlines count_store_drops into this body instead of calling it out of line. The +43 B is that inlined drop tally (a cold, drops-nonzero path). The always-inline dispatch_edge body inside fan_out is unchanged (fan_out 1893 -> 1893, +0). Priced on bench_lean_value_path: the new local-handler row at K=32 falls ~1,760 -> ~1,190 ns (16 B), 1 block / 40 B per publish unchanged. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 555 -> 384 (-171 B; hot body 519 -> 384 B, 128 -> 99 instructions, and the 36 B `.cold` clone is gone) by RFC-0028 slice 4 (target adopt, D2). The target leg no longer clones the delivered value into a `rope_t` and hands it to `store_value(rope_t&&)`: it calls the new adopting overload `store_value(vertex_t*, const value_t&, ...)`, which takes one reference on the published block. Removed from this body: the `value_t::try_rope` call and its OUT_OF_MEMORY early return, the on-stack `rope_t` and its two `~rope_t` calls (hot + the unwind pad that was the whole `.cold` clone). The call set is otherwise identical (`deref_vertex_slot`, `find_ptr`, `acl_allows`, `store_value`, `count_store_drops`, `value_t::release`). The clone did not disappear for the two shapes that cannot adopt (a HANDLER target, a caller-owned `value_storage_t`): it moved INTO the adopting `store_value`, which is not pinned and not on the stored-target arm. `edge_view_t` is 48 B and `fan_out`'s instruction stream is identical modulo `.cold` addresses, so `dispatch_edge`'s always-inline per-edge body is unchanged. A SHRINK, re-pinned as the new floor. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 627 -> 555 (-72 B) by RFC-0028 slice 3 (`value_t` replaces the LKV wrapper). The delivery clone changed from `try_clone_rope(rope_t&, const rope_t&)` — `rope_t::concat` inlined as one `.isra` call — to `value_t::try_rope`, which is `[[gnu::noinline]]` for exactly this symbol: inlined, its reserve-then-append loop made the function 692 B (+101); out of line it is one call and the body loses the `shared_ptr` release of the returned `store_value` handle (`_Sp_counted_base::_M_release`) for a one-word `value_ref_t` decrement whose teardown arm is the cold `value_t::destroy`. `edge_view_t` is 48 B, `dispatch_edge` is +0. A SHRINK, re-pinned as the new floor. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 595 -> 627 (+32) by the admission seam: this leg's store failure is no longer always a resource event, so it reads the status instead of assuming one. The old code discarded the result and counted OUT_OF_MEMORY unconditionally; a target's admission filter can now refuse a delivery, which is a POLICY refusal and belongs in `denied` beside the fan-in ACL denial counted a few lines above. The +32 B is that one `expected` compare and its branch, and the attribution is DIRECT rather than inferred: reverting only this hunk in a clean tree restores 595 B exactly, with every other pin here unmoved. Priced as a correctness-of-attribution trade — a counter that reads a rejected value as an exhausted node is worse than 32 B on a leg that is already noinline and off the wide-fan-out arm. The #1448 record this note replaces stands: at 595 B that pin was flat while the instruction stream moved 138 -> 148, which is why the two `e.caller()` reads on this leg are still deliberately not hoisted.

RE-PINNED 955 -> 1115 (+160 B, 224 -> 252 instructions) by RFC-0028 slice 4. NOT new work: `snapshot_edges` does not touch a value, and its source is unchanged. It is the same INLINE-BUDGET FLIP slice 3 recorded below, one notch back the other way: graph.cpp's TU lost `try_clone_rope`, the rope clone and its unwind pad in `dispatch_edge_target` (-171 B), GCC re-partitioned the TU's unit-growth budget, and the one out-of-line `std::_Sp_counted_base::_M_release()` call this body made is now INLINED (the call count goes 1 -> 0 and `_M_release_last_use_cold` 1 -> 2 — the inlined copy's cold tail). The +160 B is exactly that inlined atomic decrement and its branch; every other call (`copy_published` x2, `segment_ptr_t::reset` x4, `operator delete` x4, the hazard `mutex::lock`) is unmoved. An inlined release trades a call for its body on a once-per-fan-out path (not per edge), priced on the interleaved A/B in the PR. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 843 -> 955 (+112 B, 199 -> 253 instructions) by RFC-0028 slice 3. NOT new work: `snapshot_edges` does not touch a value, a `value_ref_t` or the LKV slot, and its source is unchanged. It is the INLINE-BUDGET FLIP this file already documents for `fan_out` (#1461) and `copy_published` (#1442): graph.cpp's TU lost the `std::shared_ptr` control-block machinery and the `rope_t` clone paths, GCC's unit-growth budget re-partitioned, and the same call set (`copy_published` x2, `segment_ptr_t::reset` x4, `operator delete` x4, `_Sp_counted_base` x2, the hazard `mutex::lock`) now sits under two more `lock xadd` refcount legs inlined where a shared helper was, +18 `mov` / +6 `cmp` of the same sequences duplicated across the inline and overflow arms. The value it moved by is itself budget-sensitive: an earlier cut of the same change measured 1115 B here. Priced on the bench, interleaved A/B best of 3 rounds pinned to one core on a host at load avg 60-100: `bench_libtracer fan` (the snapshot_edges-dominated sweep) inproc fan 16/64/128/256/1024 is +24.9/+10.3/+16.5/+26.8/+5.6 % deliv/s with p50 -23/-19/-7/-6/-5 %, fan 8/32 -5.3/-1.3 % (inside the same-host A/A null, which spanned -9.7..+5.6 %). Neutral to favourable; the growth is not paid for in time. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 923 -> 843 (-80, 210 -> 199 instructions) by #1448. This is the -O3 WRAPPER, not the copy loop (see the `copy_published` note) — what it inlines is the entry `inline_buf.clear()` / `overflow.clear()` pair, which DESTROYS `edge_view_t`s, and those lost two `std::string` and two `view_t` members. The instruction histogram says exactly that: the inlined refcount-release legs collapse (`xchg` 6 -> 1, `lock` 5 -> 3) and the branches they were guarded by go with them (`je` 18 -> 12, `jmp` 10 -> 6), against two more `call`s where the remaining release is now outlined. A shrink, in the same direction and from the same cause as `copy_published`.

RE-PINNED 1707 -> 1871 (+164 B, 399 -> 442 instructions) by RFC-0028 slice 3. Same INLINE-BUDGET FLIP as `snapshot_edges` above, same evidence: the source of `copy_published` and `copy_entry` is untouched and the call set is identical (`_Sp_counted_base` x2, `operator new`/`delete` x2, the length_error and catch legs) — the delta is +20 `mov`, +6 `movzbl`, +3 `pxor`/`xor`, one more `lock xadd`: the `edge_view_t` construct-and-move sequence emitted once per arm (inline buffer / reserved overflow) where the pinned build shared one copy. Per-edge work is unchanged: four words and two refcounts, no branch on the edge shape. Priced on the same `bench_libtracer fan` A/B as `snapshot_edges` (this symbol is its copy loop): neutral to favourable across the fan-out sweep. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 3554 -> 1707 (-1847 B, 761 -> 399 instructions) by #1448 — the change this pin was set to watch, arriving as a HALVING. `edge_view_t` stopped owning the cold half's bytes and started holding a `remote_ptr_t` share of it, so the per-entry copy is four words and two refcounts with no branch on the edge shape. What left the loop: the two `tr::detail::try_assign` probe-then-commit windows and their OOM unwind, the two `view_t` clone legs, and the whole per-edge `false` return path (`copy_published` no longer has a per-edge OOM tally — nothing on it can allocate). Instruction histogram: `mov` 301 -> 164, `call` 33 -> 12, `endbr64` 4 -> 2 (two fewer outlined helper entries). Priced on `bench_libtracer fan`, not argued from the disassembly. PREVIOUS NOTE, still the reason this symbol is pinned at all: ADDED by #1442. `snapshot_edges` was already pinned and stayed byte-identical (923 B, +0) across that change — but at -O3 it is only the wrapper: the pinned reader's ACTUAL copy loop is emitted out of line as `copy_published`, and it moved 4157 -> 3554 B (-603, 866 -> 761 instructions) with the pin set blind to it. `try_copy_published`'s source is untouched by #1442; the movement is an inlining-heuristic shuffle triggered by `pub_edge_t::remote` changing type from `std::unique_ptr<pub_remote_t>` to the intrusive `remote_ptr_t` (one `edge_view_t` move constructor outlined, and two `view_t::operator=` legs re-emitted as `segment_ptr_t::reset` calls). It is a SHRINK, and it was priced on the bench rather than argued from the disassembly: fanout-1 and the wide fan-out arms of bench_libtracer were within the same-window A/A null. Pinned here so the next such move is seen at review time instead of by hand.

RE-PINNED 1573 -> 1893 (+320 B) by #1461/#1462 (the receiver-owned STREAM ring). The growth is an INLINE-BUDGET FLIP, not new work on the fan-out path, and it is attributed at instruction level: `std::vector<edge_view_t>::~vector()` — one `call` in the pinned build — is now emitted INLINE at fan_out's cleanup paths, which is the whole delta (5 `operator delete` + 4 `segment_ptr_t::reset()` call sites where there were 1 and 2). It sits on the WIDE-fan-out teardown, below the no-subscriber gate and outside the per-edge loop; the per-edge dispatch body is unchanged, still one indirect callback call plus the two noinline legs, and `dispatch_edge_target` / `dispatch_edge_remote` / `snapshot_edges` / `copy_published` are all byte-identical (+0). The trigger is graph.cpp's own inline estimate moving: `store_value` gained the receiver-ring admission branch and `vertex_t::store` lost its STREAM fork, which re-partitioned the TU's budget — the same class of flip #1250 documents, in the other direction. PRICED ON THE BENCH before landing, as this gate's message demands: `inproc` 64 B / fan 1024 — the fan_out-dominated gated point — best of 3 rounds, interleaved A/B on one host under load avg ~22-39, is 7840 ns p50 against the pinned build's 8100 ns (-3.2%) and 126380 deliv/s against 122303 (+3.3%). Neutral to favourable, so the larger encoding is not paid for in time. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1613 -> 1573 (-40 B, 364 -> 361 instructions) by #1448. `fan_out` owns the `edge_snapshot_t` stack buffer and the thread-local overflow vector, both of which are arrays of `edge_view_t` — 160 B -> 48 B — so its frame setup and the two `for (const edge_view_t& e : ...)` strides re-encode against smaller displacements and a smaller stack reservation. The per-edge `dispatch_edge` body is unchanged apart from the remote-leg gate becoming `has_remote_leg()`, which is the same one load and one branch it was as `link.empty()` for the in-process edge that dominates a fan-out. The two reclamation bindings are unaffected: this pin measures the DEFAULT build, as the note below insists. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1474 -> 1613 (+139) by #894 (ADR-0080 reclaim_local). The ONLY pinned symbol this change moves — the other four are byte-identical — and the growth is fully attributed at instruction level: ONE `addl $1,%fs:` on entry, plus a 5-instruction exit epilogue emitted THREE times (the wide TLS-buffer path, the small/stack path, and the .cold unwind clone), plus `nop` re-padding and two cleanup-frame displacement changes that add no instruction. The per-edge dispatch loop body is byte-identical, so the cost is once per fan_out regardless of subscriber count, and the no-subscriber early return is untouched. Priced on the bench: `inproc-batch` fanout-1 (the batch-calibrated bare-notify case) 102 ns -> 102 ns p50, +0.00%, against a same-day A/A null of +/-0.8%. rv32 (-Os, GCC 15.2) is +24 B and +6 instructions on entry; `reclaim_strict` is +0 instructions here. NOT RE-PINNED by #1376 (reclaim_qsbr): this pin measures the DEFAULT binding, which stays at 1613 B (+0) — verified, and backed by object-file identity of graph.cpp.o's whole instruction stream against the pre-#1376 tree. For reference only and explicitly NOT gating: a build that BINDS reclaim_qsbr_t measures 1819 B here (+206), all of it the outermost-bracket announce, the exit epilogues' offline store and the drain early-out, emitted at each of fan_out's exit paths. The per-edge dispatch loop body is instruction-identical between the two bindings, and the announce sits below the no-subscriber gate, so neither a wide fan-out nor an unsubscribed publish pays for it. A QSBR size must never be pinned into this file: the gate runs the default build.

RE-PINNED 318 -> 350 (+32 B) by RFC-0028 slice 7 (one callback idiom, D10). The remote leg's source is untouched; the same slice-7 TU re-partition (the per-handler rope clone leaving graph.cpp) lets GCC 13.3 inline segment_ptr_t::reset() here in place of the out-of-line call. The +32 B is that inlined release, which is the pin value this leg had before slice 3 (350). fan_out +0. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 350 -> 318 (-32 B) by RFC-0028 slice 3. The remote leg hands the sink `const value_t&` instead of `const rope_t&`; nothing is cloned on this leg either way, and the shrink is the `rope_t` argument plumbing that is no longer there. A SHRINK, re-pinned. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 318 -> 350 (+32) by the admission seam, and NOT by any edit to this function or to the leg that calls it — an inline-budget flip of the same genre as the 298 -> 318 re-pin before it. Bisected in a clean tree, one file and then one declaration at a time: applying `vertex.hpp` alone produces 350 B with `graph.cpp` pristine, and deleting just the two new `std::function` members from the PUBLIC `handlers_t` — the by-value registration struct, now 64 B wider — puts it back at 318 with everything else in place. So the cause is the width of a registration-time parameter type re-partitioning this TU's inline budget, not anything on the delivery path: nothing this function does changed, and the code around it was re-laid-out. The filters themselves are deliberately NOT on the vertex (see `graph_t::admissions_`), so no per-vertex memory probe moves.

RE-PINNED 2939 -> 2620 (-319 B) by RFC-0010 Amendment 2 (#1503 residual). An INLINE-BUDGET re-partition of fwd_router.cpp, not a change on the forward path: the TU gained `fwd_router_t::sample_stats` — a cold, out-of-line census sampler reached only from a `:stats` field READ, never from a frame path — and GCC re-partitioned the TU's inline estimate around it, exactly the class of flip #1250 documents. Nothing this template instantiates was edited: the forward hop's decode, dst-shrink/src-grow and scatter-gather send are source-identical, and every graph-side pin above is byte-identical (+0). A SHRINK, so it is re-pinned to hold the new floor. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 2231 -> 2939 (+708) by #1503 step 3 (the router's counted cold drops). The growth is BLOCK PLACEMENT, not work: the four drop sites this hop owns now call one `[[gnu::noinline, gnu::cold]] fwd_router_t::count_drop`, and `cold` makes GCC re-partition the function's blocks around those calls at -O3 — the arms are relocated and the cold clone re-emitted, which the ratchet measures as this symbol's span. Attributed by measurement, not by reading: the SAME four call sites with `noinline` alone and no `cold` measure 2359 B (+128), so 580 of the 708 bytes are the attribute's placement and 128 are the calls themselves. The forwarding body is otherwise unchanged — every bump sits on an arm (`!rebuilt`, `!rebuilt->ok()`, `!ok || cur_src.poisoned()`) the hop already branched on and already returned from. `cold` is kept because it is what the TIME says: `bench_forward_demux`, whose A/A null on the measuring host is exactly 0.0% at every point, charged +7.3%/+8.1% at 64 registered links for the first cut that inlined the `fetch_add`s, and reads +0.7% at that point with the cold helper. A control that added 56 B of dead padding to `fwd_router_t` instead cost 0.0%, which is what rules out object layout and leaves the hot hop's instruction footprint. The DEPLOYMENT profile does not pay the 708 B: on riscv32-esp-elf -Os the whole `fwd_router.cpp` TU grows +202 B and `route_handle.cpp` +116 B, and the Cortex-M0 and rv32 footprint sentinels are byte-identical to base (neither links the net plane). PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 2023 -> 2231 (+208) by #1325 car 4 (RFC-0027 forwarder). The growth is ONE pass-through `std::span` — §6.1's minted reply-leg spelling — threaded into the three `[[gnu::flatten]]` `rebuild_fwd_forward` instantiations this hop inlines. Two cheaper shapes were measured and rejected: deciding the mint inside this hop cost +688 B, and a lazy supplier closure still cost +512 B; hoisting the decision to `route_fwd_ingress` (unpinned, and already switching on `kind`) leaves only the forwarded span. No new work executes on the request path: the `if (!is_reply)` branch that guarded the mount-run assignment became an `is_reply ? ... : ...` select on the same field. NOT priced on the bench yet — RFC-0027 §12.4 (car 5) is the gate that must, including the mandatory four-link reply-spread arm.
